newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal - Basis mixed, supplies grow.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal - Basis mixed, supplies grow.

text.p: Basis offers in U.S. cash markets for soybean meal were mixed Friday, with some pressure tied to an increase in the supply of soymeal and tepid domestic interest, dealers said.
"This is a really patchy market," said one Tennessee-based broker. "In some spots demand is pretty good, and other places it's really slow."

The National Oilseed Processors Association on Thursday reported a weekly crushing pace of 30.73 million bushels. That figure exceeded trade estimates which ranged from 29.6 to 30.4 million and surprised some brokers.
"Evidently demand is good somewhere or they wouldn't be crushing at that level," one broker said.
The cash market was also rife with rumors that a commercial company had booked a sizable chunk of export business to China.

The firm was set to export 50,000 tonnes of U.S. soybean meal for February shipment, and was said to have booked another 150,000 tonnes out of South America for shipment during May through September, traders said.
